The activity affects card C06220-K1 belonging to customer C06220, as well as 14 other cards across different customers who share this transaction template without sharing devices. The pattern was identified following an analyst request to investigate transaction 3660127 and search for related activity across other cards.

case.summary: This alert was triggered by an analyst request to review transaction 3660127 on card C06220-K1 and investigate related activity on other cards. The primary finding indicates that the same transaction template appears on 14 other cards within 14 days without sharing a device with this card, pointing to coordinated abuse across customers. The case has been assigned a verdict of fraud with a fraud probability of 0.97. Final actions include blocking the card, creating a case, filing a report, monitoring connected cards, and escalating the case to an analyst.

sar.narrative: This narrative pertains to unauthorized credit card activity identified under case HHF-002 involving customer C06220 and visa credit card C06220-K1. Between January 17, 2017, and January 19, 2017, an unauthorized party conducted three fraudulent online transactions totaling $2,166.71 on the customer's card. The first transaction, transaction 3660125, occurred on 2017-01-17 at 19:58 for $637.13 in billing region 330 using device SM-J700T1 | iOS 11.1.2 | mobile safari 11.0 | 2048x1536 under product code C. The second transaction, transaction 3660126, took place on 2017-01-18 at 19:48 for $758.80 in billing region 384 using device SM-J700T1 | iOS 11.1.1 | mobile safari 11.0 | 2048x1536 under product code C. The final flagged transaction, transaction 3660127, was processed on 2017-01-19 at 18:18:58 for $770.78 in billing region 126 from device profile SM-J700T1 | | | under product code C. These transactions were executed through bursts of online purchases from devices new to the account operating behind an anonymous proxy. When contacted, the cardholder stated they did not make the transaction(s), did not share the card details, and still has the card. The identified activity is suspicious because the observed pattern matches none of the documented fraud typologies. Furthermore, this identical template of product C purchases of $200 or more in bursts from new devices behind an anonymous proxy appeared across 14 other cards within 14 days, including cards C00450-K1, C02342-K1, C03528-K1, C05061-K1, C05704-K2, C05770-K1, C06962-K2, and C07212-K2. Notably, none of these connected cards shared a physical device with card C06220-K1, indicating coordinated abuse across multiple customer accounts.
